page: Amazon Web Services c5.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor with 96 virtual CPUs and 48 physical cores with hyper-threading running at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 192 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a compute-to-memory ratio of 2 GB per vCPU. It does not include local instance storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is delivered via a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c5.24xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI, which contribute to strong performance in cryptography, vector calculations, and software compilation. Memory bandwidth is also highly rated, with read-only cached operations reaching 5237.17 GB/sec. However, single-core performance and text generation speeds for large language models are relatively average or weak, reflecting its optimization for parallelized, high-throughput compute tasks rather than single-threaded speed or specialized AI generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5.24xlarge offers a high density of dedicated compute resources relative to its memory footprint, making it a viable option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory allocations or local SSD storage. It is well-suited for highly parallelized applications such as batch processing, distributed analytics, high-performance web serving, and scientific modeling. It also performs efficiently in database operations and Redis key-value stores, as evidenced by strong benchmark results in Redis SET operations.
